description:
FILED s470bv (Opus, 2026-09-06) while attributing t/op/magic.t's ROW SWAP.
NOT FIXED HERE.

THE MEASUREMENT.  t/op/magic.t's COUNT does not move -- C 176/31 at 614c6af, at
a3d6d8e, at b25afbc and on HEAD -- but its ROW SET does, exactly at b25afbc
(#1221, "the utf8:: mutators really transform").  One row starts passing and one
starts failing:

    FIXED : ENV store encodes high utf8 in SV
    NEW   : .. and the UTF-8 version is written

(measured with the runner's own key projection, PclTapAlign::rowkey_desc; the
three row sets at a3d6d8e and b25afbc differ in exactly these two lines.)

THE FAILING ASSERTION, t/op/magic.t ~line 510:

    my $name_utf8_bytes = $name_unicode;
    utf8::encode($name_utf8_bytes);
    ...
    $0 = $name_unicode;
    is( $0, $name_utf8_bytes, '.. and the UTF-8 version is written' );

perl DOWNGRADES on assignment to `$0`: what lands in the process name (and what
reading `$0` back gives) is the UTF-8 OCTET string, which is why the test
compares against an explicitly encoded copy.  PCL stores the wide string
unchanged, so the two sides differ by exactly that encoding.

WHY IT PASSED BEFORE.  `utf8::encode` was a no-op stub, so
`$name_utf8_bytes` still held the wide string and the comparison was
wide-vs-wide.  #1221 made the mutator real; the accident stopped.  This is the
s438 pattern: a fix that makes values real exposes what was passing on nothing.

FIX (sketch): the `$0` setter in cl/pcl-runtime.lisp must encode a string that
contains a character above U+00FF to its UTF-8 octets (and warn "Wide character
in $0" -- the file's neighbouring row already asserts one warning is emitted,
and that row passes today, so only the STORED VALUE is wrong).  Probe what perl
does for a string with only latin-1 high characters before writing it.

ACCEPTANCE: the three rows around magic.t:520 all pass (`warning after
assignment of wide character`, `.. and the warning is about a wide character`,
`.. and the UTF-8 version is written`), i.e. op/magic.t 176/31 -> 177/30;
a Pl/t guard row.
subject: `$0 = <wide string>` must store the UTF-8 OCTETS: PCL keeps the wide string, so t/op/magic.t's ".. and the UTF-8 version is written" fails (it passed by accident while utf8::encode was a stub, until #1221)
